objectives: Identify suspected measles in a child with fever, rash, cough, and red eyes.
Screen for complications and danger signs that require referral.
Apply infection prevention, vitamin A support, and counseling in HC III workflow.
takeaways: Fever preceding generalized rash with conjunctivitis raises measles suspicion.
Check feeding, breathing, hydration, and neurologic danger signs before outpatient plan.
Unimmunized children need both acute management and catch-up vaccine counseling after recovery.
learnCaseOverrides.blurb: A febrile child with rash and uncertain immunization status presents during a busy clinic day.

sections.title: Chief complaint
sections.text: Fever, cough, red eyes, and body rash

sections.title: Immunization history
sections.text: Caregiver is unsure if measles vaccine was received.

coach.title: Gloria has classic febrile rash features
coach.body: Use a structured approach: danger signs first, then likely measles complications.

sections.title: Focused findings
sections.text: Generalized maculopapular rash, cough, conjunctival redness, no severe respiratory distress.

coach.title: What is the best working diagnosis now?
coach.body: Pick the action-oriented label that guides management.

options.text: Suspected measles with complication screen needed
Simple skin allergy, no infectious concern
Malaria only because fever is present

question.right: Correct. Fever before rash plus cough and conjunctivitis in an under-immunized child should be managed as suspected measles until proven otherwise.
question.wrong: This pattern is not routine allergy. Missing measles suspicion delays IPC measures and complication screening.

sections.title: Complication check
sections.reveal_note: No danger signs currently, child drinking.

sections.title: Initial management
sections.detail: Vitamin A, fever control, fluids, infection prevention counseling

coach.title: Choose the best HC III plan
coach.body: Balance acute support with close follow-up and public-health awareness.

question.prompt: What is the safest immediate plan?

options.text: Provide supportive care (including vitamin A per age), counsel caregiver, and review closely for complications
Give only antibiotic eye drops and no further advice
Send home without warning signs because child is still active
Start injectable antimalarial as first-line for all febrile rash illnesses

question.right: Correct. Child is currently stable but measles complications can develop quickly, so supportive care plus explicit warning signs is key.
question.wrong: Narrow or no counseling misses early complications such as pneumonia, dehydration, or neurologic deterioration.

sections.title: Case outcome
sections.text: You identified suspected measles, applied supportive care, and prepared caregiver for danger signs.
sections.emphasis: Structured complication screening prevented false reassurance.

coach.title: Key teaching points
coach.body: For febrile rash illness in children, combine clinical measles suspicion, danger-sign screening, and caregiver counseling. Immunization catch-up should be discussed after acute illness.
